summary: Česnavičius proves purity for the Brauer group: for a regular scheme X and a closed subset Z of codimension at least 2, H²(X, G_m) → H²(X∖Z, G_m) is an isomorphism, settling the remaining mixed-characteristic p-primary case through finite-flat descent, henselian completion and perfectoid techniques, with refinements for tori and a characterization of fields of dimension at most one. Complete (cc-442dc5): every numbered statement is an item, every missing item is routed exactly once, and four findings are recorded; Proposition 2.2 is not established for noncommutative G (E1), which the main theorems do not need. Not formalised.

items.name: Exact étale pushforward for finite morphisms
items.statement: For a finite scheme morphism π, the pushforward on abelian étale sheaves is exact. This abelian case is what Propositions 2.2 (commutative specialization), 2.3 and Corollary 2.4 use.

items.name: Finite-flat H¹ injectivity (printed scope pending proof check)
items.statement: For a finite flat map of local rings R→R', an open V⊂Spec R, and a smooth affine R-group G, assume Γ(R,O)→Γ(V,O) is an isomorphism and every G-torsor on R is trivial. Proposition2.2 states H¹_et(V,G)→H¹_et(V_(R'),G) is injective.
items.note: The later uses have commutative G, where kernel-triviality suffices; they depend on h1-abelian, not on this item. No other item depends on this one. The printed proof checks only that H(V)→X(V) is surjective, which is the untwisted case. Full pointed-set injectivity for noncommutative G would also need surjectivity of the twisted maps (^P H)(V)→(^P X)(V) for G-torsors P on V that do not extend to R. This is recorded as research/blueprint/errata/PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-19.json, E1 (gap). It is an open proof gap, not a claimed counterexample.

items.statement: For strictly henselian regular local R of dimension≥2 and prime ℓ invertible in R, the absolute purity theorem gives H²(U_R,μ_ℓ)=0 in the use made by Theorem5.3.
items.note: EDC.2's smooth purity is not this Gabber absolute purity theorem.

uses.how: Uses Prime-to-residue-characteristic absolute purity input to supply the stated prerequisite in Prime-to-p part of strict-local Brauer purity.

items.name: Prime-to-p part of strict-local Brauer purity
items.statement: For the R of absolute-purity-input, H²(U_R,G_m)[ℓ]=0.

uses.how: Uses Prime-to-p part of strict-local Brauer purity to supply the stated prerequisite in Purity for the strictly henselian punctured spectrum.

items.name: Equal-characteristic p-primary purity after residue closure
items.statement: If R=k[[x₁,…,x_d]] with k algebraically closed of characteristic p>0 and d≥4, H²(U_R,G_m)[p]=0.

uses.how: Uses Equal-characteristic p-primary purity after residue closure to supply the stated prerequisite in Purity for the strictly henselian punctured spectrum.

items.name: Mixed-characteristic p-primary purity after residue closure
items.statement: If R is complete regular local of mixed characteristic (0,p), algebraically closed residue field and dimension≥4, H²(U_R,G_m)[p]=0.

uses.how: Uses Mixed-characteristic p-primary purity after residue closure to supply the stated prerequisite in Purity for the strictly henselian punctured spectrum.

items.name: Purity for the strictly henselian punctured spectrum
items.statement: For any strictly henselian regular local ring R of dimension≥2, H²_et(U_R,G_m)=0.

Uses Purity for the strictly henselian punctured spectrum to supply the stated prerequisite in Low support vanishing along the regular locus of codimension≥2.

items.name: Punctured torus H¹ over a dimension≤1 residue field
items.statement: For henselian regular local R of dimension≥2, residue field of dimension≤1, and R-torus T, H¹_et(U_R,T)=0.

items.name: Punctured torus H² over a dimension≤1 residue field
items.statement: Under local-torus-h1's hypotheses, H²_et(U_R,T)=0.

items.name: Cohomology with closed supports
items.statement: For closed Z⊂X and abelian étale sheaf F, construct H_Z^q(X,F), its local sheaf ℋ_Z^q, and the localization maps for j:X\Z→X; use the derived sections-with-support construction.

api.name: BrauerPurity.supports.api1
api.statement: Construct the long exact localization sequence with its actual maps.

api.name: BrauerPurity.supports.api2
api.statement: Compute strict-local stalks under the qc complement hypothesis.

api.name: BrauerPurity.supports.api3
api.statement: Give natural restriction/base-change maps and the local-to-global spectral sequence.

items.name: Local-to-global spectral sequence with supports
items.statement: For the closed-support étale theory used in Theorem6.1, E₂^(a,b)=H^a_et(X,ℋ_Z^b(F)) converges to H_Z^(a+b)(X,F).

uses.how: Uses Local-to-global spectral sequence with supports to supply the stated prerequisite in Low support vanishing along the regular locus of codimension≥2.

items.name: Strict-local computation of support stalks
items.statement: Under Theorem6.1's qc-complement hypothesis, the stalk of ℋ_Z^q(F) at a geometric point x is the supported cohomology over Spec O_(X,x)^sh with pulled-back support and coefficients.

uses.how: Uses Strict-local computation of support stalks to supply the stated prerequisite in Low support vanishing along the regular locus of codimension≥2.

items.name: Coniveau spectral sequence on the strict-local reduction
items.statement: For the Noetherian finite-dimensional regular scheme and closed support Z reached in Theorem6.1, the coniveau spectral sequence has E₁^(a,b)=⊕_(z∈Z,dim O_(X,z)=a) H_{z}^(a+b)(Spec O_(X,z),G_m) and converges to H_Z^(a+b)(X,G_m).

uses.how: Uses Coniveau spectral sequence on the strict-local reduction to supply the stated prerequisite in Low support vanishing along the regular locus of codimension≥2.

items.name: Low support vanishing along the regular locus of codimension≥2
items.statement: Let X be any scheme, Z a closed subscheme, and T an X-torus. Assume O_(X,z) is regular of dimension≥2 for every z∈Z and j:X\Z→X is quasi-compact. Then H_Z^q(X,T)=0 for q≤3.

items.name: Torus purity in degree 0
items.statement: Under low-support-vanish's exact hypotheses, H^0_et(X,T)→H^0_et(X\Z,T) is an isomorphism.
items.note: X need not be globally Noetherian or regular away from Z.

items.name: Torus purity in degree 1
items.statement: Under low-support-vanish's exact hypotheses, H^1_et(X,T)→H^1_et(X\Z,T) is an isomorphism.
items.note: X need not be globally Noetherian or regular away from Z.

items.name: Torus purity in degree 2
items.statement: Under low-support-vanish's exact hypotheses, H^2_et(X,T)→H^2_et(X\Z,T) is an isomorphism.
items.note: X need not be globally Noetherian or regular away from Z.

items.statement: Under low-support-vanish's exact hypotheses, H³_et(X,T)→H³_et(X\Z,T) is injective.

items.name: Purity for G_m across a codimension-at-least-two regular closed subset
items.statement: For locally Noetherian X and closed Z such that O_(X,z) is regular of dimension≥2 for every z∈Z, restriction H²_et(X,G_m)→H²_et(X\Z,G_m) is an isomorphism.

items.name: Generic injectivity condition for torus H²
items.statement: For Noetherian integral regular X with function field K and X-torus T, require H²_et(V,T)→H²_et(K,T) injective for every nonempty open V⊂X.

api.name: BrauerPurity.generic_injective_torus.api1
api.statement: State the condition for all opens, not only X.

api.name: BrauerPurity.generic_injective_torus.api2
api.statement: Identify images in H²(K,T) only after proving the relevant injectivity.

api.name: BrauerPurity.generic_injective_torus.api3
api.statement: Pull the condition back to a nonempty open and its function field.

Uses Generic injectivity condition for torus H² to supply the stated prerequisite in Generic injectivity for flasque tori.

items.name: Mayer–Vietoris for two open subschemes
items.statement: For opens U,V⊂X and an X-torus T, the restriction-difference map fits into the sequence H²(U∪V,T)→H²(U,T)⊕H²(V,T)→H²(U∩V,T)→H³(U∪V,T).

uses.how: Uses Mayer–Vietoris for two open subschemes to supply the stated prerequisite in Codimension-one intersection formula for torus H².
Uses Mayer–Vietoris for two open subschemes to supply the stated prerequisite in Generic H² injectivity fails for arbitrary tori.

items.name: Codimension-one intersection formula for torus H²
items.statement: For Noetherian integral regular X with function field K and X-torus T satisfying generic-injective-torus, H²_et(X,T) is the intersection over height-one x of the images of H²_et(O_(X,x),T) inside H²_et(K,T).

uses.how: Uses Codimension-one intersection formula for torus H² to supply the stated prerequisite in Codimension-one intersection formula for the Brauer group.

items.name: Codimension-one intersection formula for the Brauer group
items.statement: For Noetherian integral regular X with function field K, H²_et(X,G_m)=∩_(height(x)=1) H²_et(O_(X,x),G_m) inside H²_et(K,G_m).

uses.how: Uses Codimension-one intersection formula for the Brauer group to supply the stated prerequisite in Global residue exact sequence with bad primary parts excluded.

items.name: Flasque torus in the source convention
items.statement: For a torus split by a finite étale Galois connected cover X'→X with group Γ, its character lattice M is flasque when Ext¹_(Z[Γ])(M,Z[Γ/H])=0 for every subgroup H≤Γ, in the extension-by convention of Remark6.3.

api.name: BrauerPurity.flasque.api1
api.statement: Match the source's extension direction and the standard Tate-cohomology characterization before implementation.

api.name: BrauerPurity.flasque.api2
api.statement: Show direct factors of restriction-of-scalars split tori satisfy the condition.

api.name: BrauerPurity.flasque.api3
api.statement: Prove independence of the chosen splitting cover.

uses.how: Uses Flasque torus in the source convention to supply the stated prerequisite in Generic injectivity for flasque tori.

items.name: Generic injectivity for flasque tori
items.statement: For Noetherian integral regular X and a flasque X-torus T in Remark6.3's sense, generic-injective-torus holds.

items.name: Real norm-one torus
items.statement: Over R define T=ker(Norm:Res_(C/R)G_m→G_m); pull it back to P¹_R. The norm sequence defines a T-torsor over G_m⊂P¹_R.

api.name: BrauerPurity.norm_torus.api1
api.statement: Construct the norm map and its kernel with base change.

api.name: BrauerPurity.norm_torus.api2
api.statement: Identify real norm classes R×/N(C×)≅Z/2.

api.name: BrauerPurity.norm_torus.api3
api.statement: Track the varying fibre torsors of the norm map.

items.name: Generic H² injectivity fails for arbitrary tori
items.statement: For norm-torus, there is a nonzero element of H²_et(P¹_R,T) restricting to zero at the generic point.

items.name: Admissible Brauer residue map
items.statement: For a DVR O with fraction field K and residue k, define the residue on the ℓ-primary Brauer group to H¹_et(k,Q/Z)[ℓ∞] when ℓ≠char k, or when ℓ=char k and k is perfect; fix the map via the source's localization convention.

api.name: BrauerPurity.brauer_residue.api1
api.statement: Construct the natural residue map, not just an abstract kernel description.

api.name: BrauerPurity.brauer_residue.api2
api.statement: Prove its compatibility with restriction/localization.

api.name: BrauerPurity.brauer_residue.api3
api.statement: Record the allowed set of primes for each residue field.

uses.how: Uses Admissible Brauer residue map to supply the stated prerequisite in DVR residue exactness in the admitted primary parts.

items.name: DVR residue exactness in the admitted primary parts
items.statement: Under brauer-residue's hypotheses, 0→H²(O,G_m)[ℓ∞]→H²(K,G_m)[ℓ∞]→H¹(k,Q/Z)[ℓ∞] is exact; no terminal surjectivity is asserted.

uses.how: Uses DVR residue exactness in the admitted primary parts to supply the stated prerequisite in Global residue exact sequence with bad primary parts excluded.

items.name: Global residue exact sequence with bad primary parts excluded
items.statement: For Noetherian integral regular X with function field K, after excluding p-primary parts for each prime p for which some height-one point has imperfect characteristic-p residue field, 0→H²(X,G_m)→H²(K,G_m)→⊕_(height(x)=1) H¹(k(x),Q/Z) is exact.

uses.how: Uses Global residue exact sequence with bad primary parts excluded to supply the stated prerequisite in Higher-codimension characteristic-p points force exclusion.

items.name: Higher-codimension characteristic-p points force exclusion
items.statement: If Noetherian integral regular X has a point y of height≥2 and residue characteristic p, there is a height-one generalization x of residue characteristic p whose residue field admits a nontrivial discrete valuation, hence is imperfect. Thus the p-primary part is excluded from (6.4.4).

items.name: Field of dimension at most one
items.statement: A field k has dimension≤1 when H^i_et(k,G)=0 for all i≥2 and every commutative finite étale k-group G, and, in positive characteristic, H²_et(K,G_m)=0 for every finite separable extension K/k.

api.name: BrauerPurity.field_dimension_one.api1
api.statement: Preserve the extra positive-characteristic Brauer condition.

api.name: BrauerPurity.field_dimension_one.api2
api.statement: Relate to Serre's cohomological-dimension convention.

api.name: BrauerPurity.field_dimension_one.api3
api.statement: Prove finite separable extension stability with the appropriate Weil/Shapiro comparison.

items.statement: For k of dimension≤1 and every k-torus T, H^i_et(k,T)=0 for every i≥1.

items.statement: For a finite locally free commutative group scheme over an affine base Spec R, reuse Tau Ceti's Cartier dual obtained by finite dualization of its coordinate Hopf algebra, its contravariant equivalence, biduality and base-change comparison. This includes the field case of AppendixA.

items.statement: For a smooth commutative group scheme such as G_m or a torus, compare étale and fppf cohomology in all degrees used here; do not apply this directly to α_p or μ_p in characteristic p.

items.statement: Over a characteristic-p field, a finite commutative group scheme killed by p which is connected and whose Cartier dual is connected has a filtration with factors α_p, as used in SGA3II XVII4.2.1(ii)⇔(iv).

uses.how: Uses Connected/connected p-group devissage to supply the stated prerequisite in Dimension≤1 gives finite-flat cohomology vanishing.

items.statement: For a field k of characteristic p, H^i_fppf(k,α_p)=0 for i≥2.

items.statement: For a finite commutative k-group with étale Cartier dual, realize it as the kernel of a surjective map of k-tori via a resolution of its finite character module by lattices.

items.statement: If k has dimension≤1, then for every commutative finite k-group scheme G and every i≥2, H^i_fppf(k,G)=0.

items.statement: For a finite-type commutative group over a field, the SGA3I VIIA8.3 reduction permits passage, modulo a finite group scheme, to a smooth group, and then its finite component quotient reduces the higher-cohomology argument to a smooth connected group.

items.statement: For k of dimension≤1 and a semiabelian k-variety G, H^i_fppf(k,G)=0 for i≥2; the same finite-torsion argument treats smooth connected commutative finite-type G in characteristic zero.

items.statement: If k has dimension≤1, then H^i_fppf(k,G)=0 for every commutative finite-type k-group scheme G and i≥2.

items.statement: For p prime and a perfect field k of characteristic p, WittVector p k is a discrete valuation ring; every nonzero Witt vector is p^n times a unit.

items.statement: For a flat local homomorphism A→B of Noetherian local rings, B is a complete intersection iff A and B/m_A B are complete intersections.

items.name: Picard comparison from effective Lefschetz
items.statement: Let X be locally Noetherian, I quasi-coherent, Y=V(I), and r≥0. items.name: Finiteness theorem for local cohomology (SGA 2 VIII 2.1)
items.statement: Let X be a locally Noetherian prescheme that is locally embeddable in a regular prescheme, Y a closed part of X, F a coherent O_X-module and i an integer; put U = X - Y and c(x) = codim(closure{x} ∩ Y, closure{x}). If H^{i-c(x)}(F_x) = 0 for every x ∈ U, where H^•(F_x) is local cohomology at the maximal ideal of O_{X,x}, then H^i_Y(F) is coherent.

items.name: Depth criteria for coherence of local cohomology (SGA 2 VIII 2.3)
items.statement: Let X be locally Noetherian and locally embeddable in a regular prescheme, Y a closed part of X, F a coherent O_X-module, n an integer, U = X - Y and c as above. The following are equivalent: (i) prof F_x ≥ n - c(x) for every x ∈ U; (ii) prof F_x ≥ n for every x ∈ U with c(x) = 1; (iii) H^i_Y(F) is coherent for every i ≤ n; (iv) R^i i_*(F|U) is coherent for i < n, where i is the inclusion U → X.
items.note: Clause (iv) is the one the Lefschetz applications use. The Laszlo edition's editorial note (4) records that in the original text it appeared only inside the proof, not in the statement of the corollary.

items.name: Formal comparison of sections on a punctured spectrum (SGA 2 IX 1.4 and 1.5)
items.statement: Let A be Noetherian, separated and complete for the (tA)-adic topology for some t ∈ A, and a quotient of a regular Noetherian ring. Put X_0 = Spec A, Y_0 = V(t), let T ⊂ X_0 be closed, X = X_0 - T, Y = Y_0 ∩ X, and T' = {x ∈ X_0 : codim(closure{x} ∩ T, closure{x}) = 1}. If t is F-regular for a coherent O_X-module F and prof_{T'}(F) ≥ n+1, then the comparison morphisms of IX (1.1) are isomorphisms in degrees < n and monomorphisms in degree n. In the local case, with A local, t ∈ r(A), T = {r(A)} and n = 1: if A is Noetherian, separated and complete for the t-adic topology and a quotient of a regular ring, t is F-regular, and prof F_x ≥ 2 for every x ∈ Spec A with dim A/x = 1, then Γ(X, F) → Γ(X-hat, F-hat) is an isomorphism.
items.locator: SGA 2 IX Proposition 1.4 and Exemple 1.5; read with their proofs on 2026-09-22
items.note: The comparison theorem IX 1.1 behind 1.2–1.4 is proved by a Mittag-Leffler argument on the graded modules of IX §1 together with EGA 0_III 13.3.1; that layer has not been read.

uses.how: Uses the formal comparison of sections to identify Γ(U, E) with Γ(X-hat, E-hat), A being complete for the t-adic topology.

items.name: Algebraization of a coherent formal module on a punctured spectrum (SGA 2 IX 2.2 and 2.3)
items.statement: Let A be a Noetherian local ring, t ∈ r(A), and suppose A is separated and complete for the t-adic topology and a quotient of a regular ring. Put X_0 = Spec A, T = {r(A)}, X = X_0 - T, Y = V(t) ∩ X and T' = {p : dim A/p = 1}. Let ℱ be a coherent O_{X-hat}-module, J = t·O_{X-hat} and ℱ_0 = ℱ/Jℱ. If (1) t is ℱ-regular and (2) prof_{T'} ℱ_0 ≥ 2, then there is a coherent O_X-module F with F-hat ≅ ℱ.
items.locator: SGA 2 IX Théorème 2.2 and Corollaire 2.3; read with their proofs on 2026-09-22

items.name: Infinitesimal Picard obstruction sequence (SGA 2 XI 1.1)
items.statement: Let X be locally Noetherian, I a quasi-coherent ideal, Y = V(I), X_n = (Y, O_X/I^{n+1}) and P_n = I^{n+1}/I^{n+2}. The sequence of abelian sheaves on Y, 0 → P_n → O*_{X_{n+1}} → O*_{X_n} → 1, with P_n in its additive structure and the first map x ↦ 1 + x, is exact; its cohomology sequence gives H^1(Y, P_n) → Pic(X_{n+1}) → Pic(X_n) → H^2(Y, P_n) under Pic(X_n) = H^1(Y, O*_{X_n}). Consequently Pic(X-hat) → Pic(X_n) is injective for n ≥ p if H^1(Y, P_n) = 0 for n ≥ p, and bijective for n ≥ p if H^i(Y, P_n) = 0 for n ≥ p and i = 1, 2.
items.locator: SGA 2 XI §1, the exact sequence (1.1) and Proposition 1.1; read on 2026-09-22
items.note: The same sequence applied to Hom-sheaves of two invertible modules controls the functor P(X-hat) → P(Y_n); SGA 2 XI §1 states this but does not write the sequence out.

uses.how: Uses the infinitesimal Picard obstruction sequence to convert the vanishing of H^i(X, I^{n+1}/I^{n+2}) for i = 1, 2 into bijectivity of Pic(X-hat) → Pic(X_n).

items.name: Picard comparison along the formal completion (SGA 2 XI 2.1 and 2.2)
items.statement: If Lef(X, Y) holds then for every open neighbourhood U of Y in X the inverse-image functor P(U) → P(X-hat) is fully faithful, so Pic(U) → Pic(X-hat) is injective; if Leff(X, Y) holds then colim_U Pic(U) → Pic(X-hat) is an isomorphism. Hence, under Lef(X, Y) and H^1(Y, P_n) = 0 for n ≥ p, the maps Pic(X) → Pic(U) → Pic(Y_n) are injective for n ≥ p; and under Leff(X, Y) together with H^i(Y, P_n) = 0 for i = 1, 2 and n ≥ p, colim_U Pic(U) → Pic(Y_n) is an isomorphism.

items.name: Picard descent along a regular hypersurface section (SGA 2 XI 3.16 and 3.17)
items.statement: Let A be a Noetherian local ring that is a quotient of a regular ring, t ∈ r(A) an A-regular element, and suppose A is complete for the t-adic topology. Put X_0 = Spec A, Y_0 = V(t) = Spec(A/tA), x = r(A), X = X_0 - {x}, Y = Y_0 - {x}. (3.16) If (a) prof O_{X,y} ≥ 2 for every y closed in X and (b) prof A/tA ≥ 3, then Pic(X) → Pic(Y) is injective; in particular A is parafactorial as soon as A/tA is. (3.17) If moreover (c) prof O_{X,y} ≥ 3 for every y closed in Y, (d) prof A/tA ≥ 4, and (e) O_{X,y} is parafactorial for every closed point y of X that does NOT lie in Y, then Pic(X) → Pic(Y) is an isomorphism, and A is parafactorial if and only if A/tA is.
items.locator: SGA 2 XI Lemme 3.16 and Lemme 3.17, read with their proofs and with the proof of Théorème 3.13 (ii), on 2026-09-22
items.note: Hypothesis (e) of 3.17 is printed in the Laszlo edition as «pour tout y fermé de X, y ∈ Y»; the mathematics requires y ∉ Y, and this item uses the corrected form. (e) exists only to supply hypothesis 3) of XI Proposition 3.12, which asks for parafactoriality at the points of X - U for the open neighbourhoods U of Y; those are exactly the closed points of X outside Y, while the points of Y lie in every such U, so the printed reading would leave 3.12 unusable. The verification of (e) inside the proof of 3.13 (ii) covers every closed point of X and so does not distinguish the two readings. The 1968 North-Holland original was not consulted, so this is recorded as a reading correction to the edition read, not as a finding about Česnavičius's paper.

items.name: Spectral-space limit of an affinoid Tate system (Scholze, diamonds, 6.4 (o))

Then |X| → lim_i |X_i| is a homeomorphism of spectral spaces.

items.statement: Let A be Noetherian and complete for (t), I⊂A an ideal, J⊂A[X₁,…,X_N] finitely generated and H_B⊂H_Jac. Choose k with A[t∞]∩t^kA=0. If H_B(a)⊃(t^h), J(a)⊂t^nI and n>max(2h,h+k), there is b−a∈t^(n−h)I A^N with J(b)=0.

items.name: Elkik approximation over a Noetherian complete pair
items.statement: Let A be Noetherian and a-adically complete, B=A[X₁,…,X_N]/J finite type and H_B⊂H_Jac. For every h there are n₀,r such that n>n₀, H_B(a₀)⊃a^h and J(a₀)⊂a^n imply an exact root b≡a₀ mod a^(n−r).
